newsitem.title: CROATIA: Most Croatian stocks seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: Most Croatian stocks seen falling further.

text.p: Most Croating shares are set to ease further and only some blue chip shares and hoteliers have potential to post gains, traders said.
Shares on the Zagreb bourse were mixed on Wednesday and traders said losing shares had not yet hit the bottom.
"Most shares haven't reached their minimum yet, and will probably continue losing value," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage.
"Only Zagrebacka Banka, which is expected to gain, has the chance of breaking the trend," he added.
Zagrebacka, the leading Croatian commercial bank, gained 40 kuna to close at 1,020 on a big volume of 6,230 shares.
Another blue chip, drug firm Pliva, was also among the gainers closing 152 kuna higher at 13,652 with 456 units sold.
"Pliva oscillates plus-minus eight percent, but that does not mean much in a volatile market like ours," Kos said.
Hoteliers Istraturist and Laguna were also up, reversing the general slide of the past weeks. They both rose 50 kuna to 220 and 1,100 kuna respectively on a modest volume.
"The hoteliers' shares at their present price are still not interesting for a serious investor. They still haven't hit the bottom," Kos said.
Food processor Podravka rose seven kuna to 237 selling 1,617 shares.

Hotelier Jadranturist and Suncani Hvar, confectioner Kras and cable maker Elka were among the losers, while hotelier Arenaturist, shipping company Jadroplov and Karlovacka Pivovara brewerey stayed flat.
Turnover eased to 13.4 million shares from 48,402 shares on Tuesday.
